newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican construction mogul escapes kidnap bid.
newsitem.headline: Mexican construction mogul escapes kidnap bid.

text.p: A prominent Mexican businessman escaped a kidnapping attempt by armed men on Tuesday in central Mexico City, a television programme said.
Antonio Gutierrez Cortina, a top executive with construction firm Gutsa, got away from his assailants when his driver outmanoeuvred the kidnappers' vehicle, the programme said.
"I saw four or five people, armed with UZI-type submachineguns," Gutierrez's driver said, according to a taped interview played by the programme. The driver declined to be named or filmed.
The assailants opened fire on the armoured Mercedes-Benz car in which Gutierrez was riding but he escaped unhurt, 24 Horas said, showing images of the vehicle with several bullet holes.
No more details were immediately available.

Gutsa is a 53-year-old family company which is one of Mexico's big names in construction and infrastructure projects. The company was the main developer of Mexico City's giant new World Trade Centre building.
